NVDA.headline: Shares up 2.39% as AI rally lifts chipmakers; board partner report
NVDA.summary: NVIDIA shares rose 2.39% to 216 USD, helped by an AI-driven rally on Wall Street and strong moves in Asian chip stocks. A TweakTown report, based only on a feed summary, says board partners can no longer order GeForce RTX 5090 GPUs; the reason and scope are unknown and Nvidia has not commented. Meta's planned $95bn stock offering, with Nvidia reportedly a potential cornerstone investor, is also in the news. Shares are down 5.62% over one month.

MSFT.headline: Shares up 1.54% amid reports of voluntary buyouts for about 60,000 staff
MSFT.summary: Microsoft shares rose 1.54% to 532.6 USD in a broadly higher market. Microsoft has said it will offer voluntary exit packages to eligible staff in selected parts of the company, reportedly around 60,000 people or a quarter of its global workforce, in the US, UK, India and Canada. It follows an April retirement offer and a July Xbox layoff of 3,200. The company reports earnings later this week.

AAPL.headline: iPhone Duo display issue reports; Apple shares down 1.1%
AAPL.summary: Apple shares fell 1.1% to 343.91 USD. Reports say Apple has acknowledged inner display failures on a small number of iPhone Duo units and will offer replacements via AppleCare, though the cause and scale are not confirmed by Apple. A separate report claims Apple denied warranty cover for one unit. Other news includes a weaker Indian smartphone market and the expected launch of new Macs and an iPad mini, plus Jay-Z confirmed as Super Bowl halftime headliner.

GOOGL.headline: Shares down 1.06%; Gemini 4 Argon launch and Anthropic IPO in focus
GOOGL.summary: Alphabet shares fell 1.06% to 316.8 USD. Coverage of the new Gemini 4 Argon model focuses on its suitability for complex tasks rather than everyday use. Anthropic's filing, which shows a $80.7bn loss in the first half of the year, is also in the news. A Germany court injunction over AI Mode search statements is provisional. Shares are down 7.57% over one month.

AMZN.headline: Shares up 0.44%; reports of AI servers waiting on power
AMZN.summary: Amazon shares rose 0.44% to 249.09 USD. A Yahoo Finance piece reports some newly installed AI servers are waiting to be switched on due to power constraints, with 29 October flagged as a date for progress; details are not available. Other coverage includes a reported contractor dismissal in Japan and broader debate on whether AI spending is delivering financial returns.

META.headline: $95bn stock offering to fund AI spending; shares down 1.88%
META.summary: Meta shares fell 1.88% to 630.56 USD. The company plans a $95bn two-part equity raise to fund AI infrastructure: a $35bn underwritten offering, with Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom reportedly interested as cornerstone investors, and a $60bn at-the-market offering of non-voting class C shares. Other coverage includes restrictions on Instagram accounts in India and the launch of Instagram on Apple TV. Shares are down 11.89% over one month.

AVGO.headline: Reported Meta $95bn stock offering could involve Broadcom as investor
AVGO.summary: The Financial Times reports Meta plans a $95bn stock offering to fund its AI expansion, with Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom reportedly acting as cornerstone investors. Only the headline and summary were available, so the terms and timing are unconfirmed. Tesco is also reportedly replacing VMware with Proxmox across its store and edge estate, per a job advert, amid a dispute with VMware. Shares rose 2.33% today, though they are down 5.84% over one month and 10.95% over one year.

TSLA.headline: US Air Force bans BYD vehicles at Japan base; Tesla linked to Samsung report
TSLA.summary: The US Air Force has banned BYD vehicles at Kadena airbase in Okinawa, citing an unacceptable security risk, as part of wider US efforts to restrict Chinese technology. A separate, thinly sourced Finimize item says Tesla and Nvidia are reportedly backing Samsung's AI chip substrate expansion, with no supporting detail available. Shares rose 5.21% today and are up 9.56% over one month, though down 14.22% over one year.

TSM.headline: Shares up 1.4%; reports of substrate capacity deals and rising Intel rivalry
TSM.summary: TSMC shares rose 1.4% to 424.37 USD. A Taiwanese report cited by Wccftech claims Nvidia, AMD and Intel have paid over $5bn to Taiwanese substrate makers to reserve capacity; the companies have not named customers. An Intel executive said Intel is only a few percent behind TSMC on performance but slower to catch up on scale. Shares are up 41.25% over one year but down 6.3% over one month.

SPCX.headline: No major news; shares slightly lower
SPCX.summary: There is no major company news in the material provided. Shares fell 0.4% to 146.9 USD. The only item is a Nike product release using a SpaceX-related name, which has little relevance to the company.

JPM.headline: No major news right now
JPM.summary: There are no recent stories or headlines for JPMorgan Chase. The shares rose 0.74% today, are down 0.76% over one month and up 7.37% over one year, trading within a 52-week range of 279.10 to 366.50 USD.
